summary: Full text of the adult Suntheanine crossover (30 adults, 200 mg nightly, 4 weeks; maker-funded) shows the designated primary clinical outcomes were not better than placebo (SDS p=0.084, PSQI total p=0.073), with only three PSQI subscales separating near p=0.05. The reviewed research does not establish a qualifying benefit for this product's assessed use: the null designated primaries are kept, the verified sleep-subscale findings in 30 adults are recorded as limited findings whose possible points await the calibration batch, and the only other source (pediatric ADHD trial) is abstract-only with no verified positive primary. The record becomes reference-only, which removes Suntheanine Evidence points from dependent products.

population.description: 30 adults aged 20-69 (9 men, 21 women; mean 48.3) without major psychiatric illness, screened by a psychiatrist.

study_contexts.study_design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial: two 4-week periods with a 2-week washout; clinical assessments (SDS, STAI, PSQI) designated primary; between-period changes compared by Mann-Whitney U.

outcomes.name: Primary stress measures, L-theanine versus placebo change: SDS p=0.084 (trend only); STAI-trait improved within the L-theanine period (p=0.006) but not shown superior to placebo.
Primary sleep (PSQI): total change versus placebo p=0.073 (trend); subscales sleep latency (p=0.0499), sleep disturbance (p=0.046) and use of sleep medication (p=0.047) improved more than placebo.
Verbal fluency and executive function improved within the L-theanine period; placebo separation only in the post hoc lower-baseline median-split subgroup (verbal fluency p=0.002).

limitations: The Methods designate clinical assessments as primary and laboratory tests as secondary. Selected subscales and posthoc subgroup findings must not be presented as universal primary-outcome superiority.
Exact preparation/population/endpoints; not generic benefit or minimum effective dose.

Small (n=30) crossover with largely within-period significance; primary stress scores were not superior to placebo and only three PSQI subscales separated at p just under 0.05 without multiplicity control.
Funded by Taiyo Kagaku, which supplied the tablets; two authors are Taiyo Kagaku employees.

No credit: the designated primary outcomes were not superior to placebo (SDS p=0.084; PSQI total p=0.073; only three PSQI subscales separated), so per the corrected brief this completed trial is non-crediting with its true directions. It does not show stress/anxiety reduction versus placebo. Returned A024 date-only restriction was withdrawn; this assessment rests on the verified full text.

Limited verified secondary finding (hierarchy kept; per Dr. Pham's fifth ruling): in 30 adults, PSQI sleep-latency (p=0.0499), sleep-disturbance (p=0.046) and sleep-medication (p=0.047) subscales improved more than with placebo. Whether limited points may rest on such findings awaits the calibration batch; they are never promoted to primary.
Context authored and source-verified by agent review (Claude) on 2026-10-28; Dr. Pham's pre-approval of fully source-verified contexts attested by Sean on 2026-10-28.

dose.administration_frequency: One 200 mg tablet orally before sleep each night for 4 weeks; 2-week washout between periods.

normalization.basis: Whole assigned material daily mass from primary Methods; not a marker or active-equivalent conversion.

source_provenance.location: Full text (PMC6836118): Methods 2.1-2.5 (participants, intervention, primary clinical assessments, statistics), Results Table 2 paragraph, Table 3 and median-split table, Funding and Conflicts of Interest.

clinical_review.notes: No credit: abstract-only (Altern Med Rev 2011, no open full text) pediatric ADHD trial; primary endpoint and statistics cannot be verified, and the population (boys 8-12 with ADHD) does not transfer to adult products.

limitations: Abstract: 98 boys aged 8-12 with ADHD; two 100 mg Suntheanine chewable tablets twice daily (400 mg/day) or placebo for 6 weeks; actigraphy sleep percentage and efficiency higher than placebo, sleep latency unchanged; parent questionnaire did not track actigraphy.
Context authored and source-verified by agent review (Claude) on 2026-10-28; Dr. Pham's pre-approval of fully source-verified contexts attested by Sean on 2026-10-28.
